title: Reel: why big clicker moves backfire
caption:
When the fork feels wrong, it's tempting to crank the clicker five at a time. Go too far in and the fork stops moving and skips off everything. Swing back too far and it blows through the travel.

One or two clicks, a couple of laps, then decide. Counted out from fully closed, one change at a time, so you know what each click did.

Tell Dialed Offroad what the bike did and it tells you which clicker, which way and how many. Link in bio.

title: Reel: what one rebound click does
caption:
The rebound clicker doesn't change how hard the fork hits. It changes how fast it comes back after. One click in closes the bleed gap a little, oil returns slower, and the fork comes back slower.

Too fast and the front feels light and deflects. Too slow and it packs down. Counted out from fully closed, one click at a time.

Tell Dialed Offroad how the front felt and it tells you which way to turn it. Link in bio.

title: Reel: fork too soft all over
caption:
A fork that dives on the brakes and bottoms on landings usually has too little compression for the rider. Oil moves through the piston too easy, so nothing holds it up in the stroke.

Go in a click or two at a time and it starts to hold up. If a few clicks don't fix it, look at the spring: clickers slow the oil, they don't carry your weight.

Tell Dialed Offroad it felt too soft and it tells you which clicker and which way. Link in bio.
